previous_rounds.prompt:
From: Ethan Jacobson <ethan.jacobson@insurity.com>
Subject: Refine should not work in the main working tree

Body:
To allow concurrent manual development by the developer, refine should always use a dedicated worktree.  I thought it did that, but apparently not.  Here is an answer from Claude when I asked about some main working tree changes that appeared:


What the changes are: the configuration-screen filter/sort feature — a "Filter by {key}" search box (config-filter-input, filterText(), onFilterChange), reworked sorting in data-grid.component.ts, and a new config-filter-and-sort.spec.ts replacing the old screen spec. That's your refine goal's work.

Where they live: only in your main working tree (/insurity/ProSuite). I checked every worktree — no refine worktree has them — and git log --all -S 'config-filter-input' finds them on no branch at all (not insurity-claims, not origin, not any refine/<id>/round-N).

Your assumption is off — this goal is running in your MAIN worktree, not a separate one. The tell: minutes ago, right after I stash-popped them, those files were unstaged ( M); now they're back to MM (staged again). Something re-staged them since — i.e., the refine goal is actively editing and staging in main right now. (You do have 7 goals isolated under .git/refine-worktrees/, so refine can use worktrees — but this particular config-screen goal is operating directly on main.)

Why they haven't been pushed: because they've never been committed. The goal is mid-round — refine only creates a commit (Implement <goal> round N) when a round completes, and only then does it land on a branch and get pushed. Until then it's live working-tree state, so there's literally nothing on origin to push.

One thing worth flagging: because this goal shares the main worktree with everything else, my push operation earlier had to stash/restore these exact files (the merge wouldn't proceed with them dirty). I restored them and the goal has since continued — so no harm done — but it means your git operations and this running goal are working in the same tree simultaneously, which is inherently race-prone. If you can, it's safer to let that goal finish its round (and commit) before doing manual git work in main, or run it in an isolated worktree like your other goals. Nothing to fix right now; the work is intact and will push itself when the round lands.


[cid:insurity-small2_2f81c33c-d951-4e5c-a467-1113541ca22c.jpg]
Ethan Jacobson
Ethan.Jacobson@insurity.com

skill.name: Quality
skill.prompt:
## Quality review

Independently review the finalized plans and candidate implementation. Select or add meaningful tests, correct defects when needed, and run the relevant checks. Report actual commands, results and findings. Refine verifies the exact candidate and supervises evaluation commands.

## Required behavior

Preserve the relevant Goal and docs/intent product behavior. Keep Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces coherent; shared capabilities authoritative; local state and evidence inspectable and recoverable; and affected surfaces semantically consistent.

## Review and verification

Judge the candidate against the Goal and only the relevant docs/intent pages. Use the smallest deterministic checks that cover the affected behavior, adding or adjusting behavior-focused tests only when evidence is missing. Scale integration and failure-path checks to actual risk. Report exact commands, results, and remaining uncertainty. Do not require unrelated tests, documentation, refactors, or cleanup; documentation is relevant only when product intent or an architectural contract changes.

## Acceptance checks

- The candidate satisfies the Goal and relevant docs/intent contracts, preserves the existing architecture and consistent behavior across affected surfaces, and passes focused deterministic regression checks.

## Intent and architecture

Applicability: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.

For this project on the current Default node, /home/buddy/projects/refine-next is the target development checkout and /home/buddy/projects/refine is the serving Refine installation. Use the invocation's pinned workspace (the managed Goal Round worktree when supplied) for code changes and verification, and read the relevant intent from that candidate. Verify paths from the current invocation and runtime before operating on another node. Source promotion and restarting the serving installation are separate operator actions; an ordinary implementation or Quality run should not deploy its candidate or restart the daemon that is supervising it.

## Cohesive code files

Applicability: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.
